entries.text: Max Nightriver pushed through the Guild crowd and read the Wendhope posting, deciding the unusually high pay meant something was wrong. Ellie registered the new party as the Ash Lanterns, and Max claimed leadership, recruiting Belle and Dalan. Tobias warned that Wendhope sits on Sheridan lands, that the fee is payment upon completion, and that the Guild offers no advance, so the party would walk if they could not afford horses. Max accepted the job, and the Ash Lanterns left Aegis at first light, riding north on the frontier road. Dalan reported the road clear but noted the soil changing as they left the farmlands for pine forest and the wilderlands ahead.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I push through the crowd to the board and read the Wendhope posting twice. "Actually, no. Not for that money. Something's wrong with a village that pays that much to be found."
Ellie: "Ash Lanterns." Ellie's pen scratches a name into the Guild's thick registration book. "Yes. The Ash Lanterns. And who is the leader?" Her eyes dart between you, Belle, and Dalan with a matchmaking glow in them before she snaps back to professionalism. "Actually, wait. Do you have any questions about the posting? Tobias is much better at the details than I am."
*She taps the ledger, then looks at Belle and Dalan, her expression softening as she takes to pairing people together.*
Max Nightriver: "I'll lead, for now." I nod at Belle and Dalan. "You two, if you want in, the Ash Lanterns ride north today. Tobias, anything we should know about Wendhope before we go?"
Tobias: "A sensible choice." Tobias's blue eyes flicker over you and the others before his hand goes to the notice. "Wendhope sits on the Sheridan lands, and the Sheridans pay well for its silence. If you are not going to investigate, then you will be going to die. The coin is above the standard D-rank fee because this is no rescue mission."
*He pauses, the ghost of a memory on his face, before straightening his vest.* "Go prepared. Take rations for a week. The road is clear, but Wendhope itself will be a different matter."
Max Nightriver: "Rations for a week, then." I turn to Ellie. "Is there an advance on the fee? We'll need horses."
Tobias: "No." Tobias's voice is flat as he turns to Ellie. "The Guild advances nothing." He looks at you with a thin, tight line of a smile. "The Sheridan's fee is not an advance; it is payment upon completion. If you cannot afford horses, you may walk."
*His fingers drum on the ledger, the sound like a heartbeat. The scar on his left thigh twitches, unseen, beneath the black slacks.* "The Sheridans would not be fooled by a desperate party. They want results, not apologies."
Tobias: "No." Tobias's voice is sharp, but not cruel. He looks at you directly, his eyes clear and steady. "The Guild advances nothing. The Sheridan fee is payment for completion." He pauses, his voice softening. "And the Sheridans would have no interest in funding your journey. They do not fund failed parties."
*He sets down his pen, his blue eyes watching you. The memory of his old party's flash in his eyes before he vanishes.* "If you cannot afford horses, the road is clear enough for your feet."
Max Nightriver: I sigh and look back at the board. "Fine, we'll do it. Ash Lanterns. Let's ride north."
Adolion Narrator: Ellie's pen scribbles the name into the register, then snaps shut with a decisive click. "Ash Lanterns," she reads back, her voice bright with the sound of it being a real party at last. She looks at you, then Belle, then Dalan, and then at Tobias, her matchmaking glow dimming just a little. "Tobias, I'll mark it D-rank."
Tobias gives a short, sharp nod. He reaches over and pulls the Wendhope notice from the board, rolling it up and handing it to you. "Your posting." His voice is flat, business-like, but there is something behind it, something older than the current moment. "Do not fail."
The Guild's hall is still loud, full of people who are still waiting for their turn or still looking for a posting, and the air smells of stale ale and old sweat. You have a notice in your hand and two new allies by your side, and all that you know is that Wendhope sits on the Sheridan land in the north and that the Sheridans will pay well for its silence, and that Tobias and Ellie have given you their warnings.
You are the Ash Lanterns, and you ride north today.
Max Nightriver: We leave Aegis at first light and follow the frontier road north. "Dalan, Belle, keep your eyes open. Tell me if anything about this road feels wrong."
Dalan: Dalan's ears twitch as he rides, eyes scanning the tree line. "Nothing yet. Road's clear, and the birds aren't spooked." He glances at you with a thoughtful look. "But the soil's changing. We're leaving the farm lands."
*He pulls his horse's reins tight as the land shifts to sandy soil, and then into pine forest and a dark, treeline.* "The wilderlands are ahead. If we're going to run into trouble, it'll be here."

Belle: Belle shifts in her saddle, her greataxe Cleaver leaning against her shoulder as she rides. "Birds don't mean shit." She scans the horizon with her brown eyes, looking for anything that could break the morning quiet. "But I've seen what happens when a road gets too quiet. canon.prose:
Max Nightriver read the Wendhope posting at the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and refused it at first, suspecting something wrong with a village paying so much. Ellie registered the new party as the Ash Lanterns, and Max took the lead, recruiting Belle and Dalan. Tobias warned them the job was no rescue mission and offered no advance, so the party left Aegis at first light, riding north until the farmland gave way to pine forest and the wilderlands.

Belle rode alongside her companion, greataxe Cleaver resting on her shoulder as she scanned the quiet morning horizon. She warned that a silent road often meant something was waiting for the unwary, and promised to stay alert until told to swing. The tone was wary and steady, braced for trouble.

[WORLD INFO CURATION TASK — output structured lines only. Do NOT continue the roleplay.]
You keep a story's own lorebook honest as play moves on: switch entries on when they now matter, off when they no longer do, and correct text the story has overtaken.
STORY: Adolion: The Adventurer's Road
WHERE THE STORY IS: The Guild Hall — Take a posting and form a party.
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Anchor guild-hall: Take a posting and form a party.
Fact(3): The party is named the Ash Lanterns, with Max Nightriver as leader.
Fact(3): Ellie registered the new party as the Ash Lanterns, with Max Nightriver as leader, and Belle and Dalan joining.
Fact(3): The party is named the Ash Lanterns, with Max Nightriver as leader, and Belle and Dalan joining.
Fact(3): Ellie registered the new party as the Ash Lanterns, with Max Nightriver as leader, and Belle and Dalan joining.
Fact(3): The Ash Lanterns have formally taken the D-rank Investigate Wendhope posting, and Tobias handed Max the rolled notice.
Fact(3): The Ash Lanterns were formally registered and took the Wendhope posting; Tobias handed Max the rolled notice and said 'Do not fail.'
Fact(3): The Guild advances no coin; the Sheridan fee is payment only upon completion, so the party must walk north without horses.
Fact(3): The Ash Lanterns left Aegis City at first light and are following the frontier road north toward Wendhope.
OPEN THREADS:
- The Ash Lanterns must prepare for the road north — a week of rations and no horses, since the Guild advances nothing.
- Tobias's unspoken memory tied to Wendhope and the Sheridan lands remains unexplained.
- The Ash Lanterns must decide whether to take the Wendhope posting despite Max's suspicion that the high fee hides something wrong.
- Tobias's scar and the flash of his old party when the Sheridans are mentioned suggest a personal history with Wendhope or the Sheridan lands that he has not explained.
- The Ash Lanterns must survive the road north and the unknown danger at Wendhope without horses, carrying only a week of rations.
- Tobias's warning that the party will die if they do not investigate Wendhope — and his unspoken memory of the Sheridans — remains unexplained.
- The party must survive the road north and the unknown danger at Wendhope, warned that failure means death.
- The Ash Lanterns must cross the wilderlands on the road north, where Dalan expects trouble to begin.

  content: [State of Needlehaven in this campaign. {{// so:protect}}The pine forest west of Wendhope is the source of the red fog and the Screechers.{{// so:end}} Its Lord Spirit is awake and in pain, and the forest is thick, alive and growing alabaster where the mine cut its roots.]
- #4 "Chronicle - Driftmere" (Adolion Chronicle)
  keys: Driftmere
  content: {{// so:auto}}[State of Driftmere in this campaign. The mining town is shut: Baroness Serenola has closed the workings, the miners have no income and are running out of savings, and requested Nightriver aid has not arrived. Offerings to Filwern crumble to dust.]
- #5 "Chronicle - The Driftmere Mines" (Adolion Chronicle)
  keys: Driftmere Mines
  content: [State of the Driftmere Mines in this campaign. The workings are sealed to miners and their layout changes on its own, so no map holds. Floor Bosses hold each level against intruders, and Filwern's divine wards at the bottom are cracked but standing.]
- #6 "Chronicle - House Nightriver" (Adolion Chronicle)
  keys: Nightriver, House Nightriver
  content: [State of House Nightriver in this campaign. Lord Javon rules the house coldly; his heir, Natalia and Welden carry the bloodline's seals without the younger two knowing what they are. The heir has been named the Crown's second against General Leevon, and marriages the children dread are being arranged.]
Output one line per change, at most 4:
[enable] <#number or entry title>
[disable] <#number or entry title>
[rewrite] <#number or entry title> || <the full replacement text>
[patch] <#number or entry title> || <first words of the span to replace> || <last words of that span> || <replacement text>
Then one final line: [why] <one sentence on what changed in the story that made these necessary>
RULES:
- Name each entry by its #number, or by its title exactly as listed above. Anything else is discarded.
- [enable] only an entry marked [currently off]; every other entry is already on.
- [disable] only an entry that is not marked [currently off].
- An entry marked [shown in part — patch only] may only be patched: you have not seen all of it.
- Some entries carry `{{// ...}}` bookkeeping markers. Never write, move or delete a marker, and never change the words between `{{// so:protect}}` and `{{// so:end}}`.
- Prefer [patch] over [rewrite]: quote the first and last words of the span exactly as they appear in the content.
- Keep replacement text under 600 characters. Never restate the whole entry in a patch.
- Only propose a change the story has actually made necessary. Style preferences are not changes.
- Never invent new entries, never touch anything outside the list, never write about the player's own knowledge.
If nothing needs changing, output NONE. That is the expected answer most of the time.
